paths.name: mastery adds the extension at the end

stages.name: a stage mark before the probe is finished changes nothing

chunks.name: two sentences
chunks.text: Variance is a squared quantity. Its square root, the standard deviation, is back in the original units.
expect: Its square root, the standard deviation, is back in the original units.

chunks.name: a colon ends a piece
chunks.text: Here is the idea: spread matters. It is simple.

chunks.name: a long sentence is cut after commas once a piece is long enough
chunks.text: The variance of a sample measures how far the values sit from their mean, averaged after squaring every distance so that the signs cannot cancel, which is why it is always non-negative.
expect: The variance of a sample measures how far the values sit from their mean,
averaged after squaring every distance so that the signs cannot cancel,
which is why it is always non-negative.

chunks.name: a long sentence with nowhere to cut stays whole
chunks.text: The variance of a sample measures how far the values sit from their mean averaged after squaring every distance so that the signs cannot cancel and why it is always non-negative.
expect: The variance of a sample measures how far the values sit from their mean averaged after squaring every distance so that the signs cannot cancel and why it is always non-negative.

chunks.name: no cut inside brackets
chunks.text: We write the pair as (a, b) and then, once the pair is fixed, we compute the quantity of interest by summing the squares of the entries, one at a time.
expect: We write the pair as (a, b) and then, once the pair is fixed,
we compute the quantity of interest by summing the squares of the entries, one at a time.

chunks.name: a short first clause is not cut alone
chunks.text: When you divide by n minus one instead of n, you are correcting for the sample mean, which always makes the squared distances look slightly smaller, so we repair it.
expect: When you divide by n minus one instead of n,
you are correcting for the sample mean, which always makes the squared distances look slightly smaller, so we repair it.

chunks.text: Because the mean is estimated from the same data, the deviations are slightly too small [see the note, which is short], and the fix is to divide by n minus one; then the average is unbiased.
expect: Because the mean is estimated from the same data,
the deviations are slightly too small [see the note, which is short],
and the fix is to divide by n minus one;
